reasoning: The two groups touch different parts of the skill, so most edits stay independent. Failure edits are kept. Success edits are kept only where they add a pattern the failure edits don't cover. (1) Failure #4 (acronym-letter clues) and success #3 (foreign-phrase gloss) both anchor on the '(Conch).' sentence in Rule 1, so I merged them into one insert_after to avoid an ordering conflict between a replace and an insert on the same text. (2) Success #4 (head-noun tie-breaker) is dropped as a duplicate of the failure BARE-HEAD TEST, which already says to keep a modifier only when the bare word alone would be wrong and points to the head-noun exception. (3) Following the meta guidance against overfitting and a growing skill, I removed task-specific facts and near-gold answers from the failure bullets, such as the speech-balloon example, the sabbatical-mayor detail and the 'last track on his 1983 album' phrasing. I shortened the remaining bullets so each fits in one brief reasoning line. (4) The Rule 3 archive protections and the existing verbatim-match priority are untouched. The new archive-is-exact bullet protects Rule 3 from Rule 4 trimming. (5) The 'repeats the clue with no answer' bullet and the other success bullets (bare-definition fragment, peerage-place, numeric options) cover distinct patterns and are kept, tightened. (6) Nothing targets the protected SLOW_UPDATE block.

edits.target: - When the clue says only 'one of these' / 'this <generic noun>' and the answer is a common noun, give the plain common noun with no added modifiers: 'a back shaped like one of these' -> 'Balloon' (not 'hot air balloon'). Modifiers copied from passages (hot air, synthetic, funeral, speech) are usually wrong unless part of the standard proper name.
edits.content: - BARE-HEAD TEST (for 'one of these' / 'this <generic noun>' clues, 'Term/Word/Name for ...' definitions, and 'this sport / game / instrument'): when the answer is a common noun or a sport, give the plain head word with no modifiers. 'a back shaped like one of these' -> 'Balloon' (not 'hot air balloon'); 'the ball used in this sport' -> 'Football' (not 'NFL football'). Drop modifiers copied from passages: kind words (hot air, synthetic, funeral, speech) and league, organization, country or sponsor prefixes (NFL, American, Olympic). Ask: would a trivia key accept the bare head word alone? If yes, use it. Keep a modifier only when the bare word alone would be wrong (see the head-noun exception below: 'Charley horse', 'hydrogen bomb') or when it is part of the standard proper name.

edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content: - ECHO / CO-MEMBER CHECK: a quoted title in the clue (song, album, film, book) is an anchor, never the answer; if the clue asks about the work's creator, answer the creator's name. 'X & this actor ...' or 'A and this co-star/partner/co-founder' -> the OTHER member of the pair, never the one already named. If your candidate string appears in the clue, reject it. A person slot never takes a place, ship or event name from the passages. When the clue gives an office plus a distinctive action, answer the person who did the action (use your own knowledge), not another holder of the same office whose page matches only the title.

edits.target: Before the answer tags, briefly quote the matched line.
edits.content: - An archived answer is final and EXACT. Rule 4 trimming and fuller names from encyclopedia passages do not apply to it. Keep a qualifier printed after a comma ('Anchorage, Alaska' stays as is). A one-word archive answer stays one word. In flat dumps with no delimiter, the answer is the word(s) right after the clue's last words.

edits.target: answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content:
The same applies to 'Known as "<foreign phrase>", this sport/dish/term ...': find the passage equating the foreign phrase with an English term and answer with that English generic name, not the foreign phrase or a country from the clue.
- Letter-of-acronym clues ('The second "S" in XYZS stands for this city'): spell out the full name the acronym abbreviates, assign the letters in order, and answer the word matching the letter asked. A trailing campus or branch letter names a DIFFERENT place from the flagship's home city. Use the passage that gives the full name.

edits.target: Other clue details (diet, ingredient, cooking method) are just conditions on the generic dish.
edits.content: - 'X is an ingredient in this type / kind of <noun>': the answer is the NAMED variety of that noun. Find the passage that pairs the clue's feature with a variety name. A material or descriptor adjective from the passages ('synthetic', 'natural') names no variety and is wrong. Keep the head noun when the bare modifier would not be a standard name.

edits.target: - Otherwise, build the answer from passages that match several of the clue's details.
edits.content: - A passage that only REPEATS the clue with the answer cut off (flashcard dump, quiz-title listing, search-index page) is NOT an archive hit. Do not copy a guess from it. Its title, heading or URL slug may name the topic, so use that as a hint. Then take the answer from topical passages that restate the clue's facts (year, place, number, role) or from your own knowledge, and prefer the entity that recurs beside those details over a one-off mention.

edits.target: Give the bare name ('Ronald Reagan'), not the event, the place or the date.
edits.content: - A short fragment with no 'this/he/she' (a scoring or action description, or a 'place + trait' phrase) is a bare definition. Answer with the single term or name that satisfies ALL its details: a sport or idiom term for an action or scoring description, a person for a role plus place or trait. Find the passage sentence that states the same fact and take the answer from it.

edits.target: - 'One of these <role/title>' ('the 14th one of these spiritual leaders') asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content: - Peerage or office-of-place clues ('The Marquess/Duke/Earl of this...', 'the Bishop of this') ask for the PLACE the title is tied to, not the holder's name or the rank word. Pick the place the passages pair with the clue's other facts. A quoted pun word in the clue often confirms it.

edits.target: - Clue lists its own options ('Of North Park, East Park, West Park or South Park, it's where...'): the answer is exactly one of the listed options, copied verbatim. Use the context to pick which.
edits.content: - Numeric options ('Of 2, 5 or 10, the number of ...'): test each option against the passages. If they give parts rather than one stated total, add the parts and pick the option equal to the sum, not the one matching a single component.
